questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as:

options.text: A solid red light.
A stop sign.
A yield sign.
A caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing light means stop completely. Look both ways and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The largest vehicle.
The car on the left.
The car on the right.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the right.
questions.explanation: The car on the right has the right-of-way. The car on the left must wait and go when it is safe.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Which lane should your car be in after the turn?

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: After turning left onto a one-way street, stay in the left lane. This is the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When a car on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time as you.
When your traffic light is green with a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield when coming out of a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

questions.question: Your gas pedal gets stuck open while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the engine, then apply brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine, then apply brakes and move to a safe area.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine carefully without locking the steering wheel. Then press the brakes and drive to a safe spot.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be in one place or moving (like road striping or snow removal vehicles). Orange signs mark work zones. Always slow down and pay attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does a stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop. Go when it is safe.
Proceed carefully. You do not always need to stop.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop. Go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means come to a complete stop. Yield to vehicles and pedestrians. Proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side traffic is moving on.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they can see traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: You stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe. This matches which traffic light?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to others, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. What should you do before you start moving?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children can hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When you back up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on your mirrors. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up, especially when children are near.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A red light is ahead.
The traffic signal is broken.
A green light is ahead.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up beside the car in front of the empty space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up beside the car in front of the empty space.
questions.explanation: After you find a parking space and check for traffic, pull up parallel to the car in front of the space. Then turn your wheels to begin parking.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on your right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only when they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a car that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same while on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Then reduce your speed.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross these lines to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind or ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid black HAWK signal mean?

options.text: Drivers may go forward with caution.
Drivers should slow down and get ready to stop.
Drivers must come to a complete stop.
There are no pedestrians nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may go forward with caution.
questions.explanation: HAWK signals are used at pedestrian crossings. A solid black signal means drivers may proceed through the crosswalk but should be careful.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before every lane change, turn your head to check your blind spots.

questions.question: Your car is in an accident and is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Never move your vehicle.
Wait for police to arrive before moving.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Always identify yourself and help if needed. Do not leave the scene.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has several turns and curves.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you enter a curve. Speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming vehicle has bright high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:

options.text: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side and you cannot completely cross. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.
